clue.text: Examine closely fellow in pose

indicators.note: in places the letter for fellow inside the word meaning pose

parts.note: to pose for a portrait is to sit

explanation.surface: Someone inspects a man who is striking a pose.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrutinise something carefully is to sift it, as when sifting through evidence.

clue.text: Informer shows what Wimbledon's famous for

explanation.surface: An informer is the very thing Wimbledon is best known for.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon, the London tennis championship, is played on grass courts, so its famous grass is 'super grass'. 'shows' only links the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a police informer who betrays many criminals is a supergrass; read as two words it praises the excellent lawns of the Wimbledon tennis courts.

clue.text: Meeting in class about university

indicators.note: about means the word for class goes around the letter for university

parts.note: a school class in Britain is a form

explanation.surface: A gathering held in a classroom to discuss the university.
explanation.definitionFit: A forum is an assembly or gathering for open discussion.

clue.text: Afternoon entertainment with music for French char?

definitions.text: Afternoon entertainment with music for French char?

parts.words: Afternoon entertainment with music for French char?
parts.note: a tea dance, named in French; char is British slang for tea, so the French word for it heads the name

explanation.surface: An afternoon of music laid on for a French charwoman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'char' looks like a cleaning lady or a fish, but in British slang it means tea; the French for tea plus their word for dancing names an afternoon tea dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea dance, an afternoon social with music and dancing, goes by this French name.

clue.text: Beatings that are concealed?

parts.note: thrashings, read jokingly as a plural of things that have been tucked out of sight

explanation.surface: Thrashings that are kept secret.
explanation.definitionFit: A thrashing is a hiding in British usage, and the word also suggests things that are hid.

clue.text: See me in dull surroundings, I'm unrealistic

indicators.note: in, with surroundings, puts the word me inside the word for dull

parts.note: drear is a poetic word for dull or dreary
taken as written

explanation.surface: Look at me in dreary surroundings; I have my head in the clouds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is only a link here, and 'surroundings' backs up 'in': DREAR surrounds ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with fanciful, impractical ideas is a dreamer.

clue.text: No thanks given to distinguished count

annotationWithheld.why: No thanks given to distinguished count: 'distinguished' and 'count' both define NOBLE, but no reading of 'No thanks given to' builds the letters and no source confirms the parse or a misprint
annotationWithheld.clue: No thanks given to distinguished count

clue.text: Get garage rebuilt and you may need this

definitions.text: Get garage rebuilt and you may need this

indicators.note: rebuilt says the letters of get and garage are put back together in a new order

explanation.surface: If you rebuild your garage you will need some of this material.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: rebuilding a garage calls for concrete, made with sand and gravel.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggregate is the crushed stone and gravel mixed into concrete for building work.

clue.text: Very small, flimsily made new shed

indicators.note: shed means the letter for new is dropped from the word for flimsily made

parts.note: cheap, flimsy metal goods are called tinny

explanation.surface: A newly built shed that is small and shoddily constructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a garden hut but is a verb: TINNY sheds N.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny is a synonym of minute or very little.

clue.text: Musician who may make intro sag

indicators.note: may make suggests the letters of intro and sag can be rearranged to form something else

explanation.surface: A performer whose opening might make the audience flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A church instrumentalist playing the pipe organ is a kind of musician.

clue.text: Section on ledge makes you sort of quail

parts.note: a section is a part
a ridge is a raised ledge or crest

explanation.surface: A portion of a narrow ledge would make anyone tremble with fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quail' reads as a verb, to cower on a dizzying ledge, but it is the game bird; the partridge belongs to the same family.
explanation.definitionFit: Partridge and quail are both small game birds of the pheasant family.

clue.text: Start with former Israeli Nobel peace prize winner

definitions.text: former Israeli Nobel peace prize winner

explanation.surface: Opening with an Israeli statesman who won the Nobel Peace Prize.
explanation.definitionFit: To commence is to begin; Menachem Begin, Israeli prime minister, shared the 1978 Nobel Peace Prize with Sadat.

clue.text: Dance and drink on the airline

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic drink
BA is British Airways, the UK flag-carrying airline

explanation.surface: Dancing and drinking aboard a flight.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance.

clue.text: Such is this clue — and all the rest!

definitions.text: Such is this clue — and all the rest!

parts.words: Such is this clue — and all the rest!
parts.note: every clue in the puzzle carries a figure identifying its place in the grid

explanation.surface: A remark that this clue, like every other, shares one property.
explanation.definitionFit: Each clue is given a number in the grid, so every one is labelled by figures.

clue.text: We snappers supply the press

indicators.note: supply is read as supple-ly, so the letters of we and snappers bend into a new order

explanation.surface: Photographers announce that they provide the pictures for the media.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like a verb meaning provide, but reads as the adverb of supple, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The press is the collective term for printed journalism, the daily papers.

clue.text: Talk and talk? Bob does

parts.note: talking on and on is British slang 'rabbiting on', and a man called Bob does just that

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone chatters endlessly, and answering that Bob certainly does.
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit (on) is British slang for chattering at length, from the rhyming slang rabbit and pork, talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Chattering endlessly is rabbiting in British slang.

clue.text: Ban evil fellow, one from West Indies

parts.note: to bar someone is to ban them
bad means evil
Ian is a man's name, standing for any fellow

explanation.surface: A demand to exclude a wicked man who comes from the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Caribbean island of Barbados is a Barbadian.

clue.text: A member in storm may go on this

indicators.note: in places a and the abbreviation for member inside the word for storm

parts.note: to storm is to rage
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP caught in a storm might set off on a violent spree.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works in the phrase 'go on the rampage'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rampage is a spell of violent, uncontrolled behaviour that rioters may go on.

clue.text: High-ranking public official in Orange

explanation.surface: A senior civil servant in Orange, the Dutch royal house or the French town.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior, powerful civil servant is called a mandarin in British usage; a mandarin is also a small citrus fruit like a tangerine.

clue.text: Wrinkled retainer close to a corporation?

definitions.text: Wrinkled retainer close to a corporation?

parts.words: Wrinkled retainer close to a corporation?
parts.note: an old servant near a business reads instead as a creased pouch holding the testicles, just below a pot belly

explanation.surface: An aged, lined servant who works near a big company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporation' is old humorous slang for a large paunch, and the retainer is what holds something in place, not a servant.
explanation.definitionFit: The scrotum is the wrinkled pouch of skin that holds the testes, below the belly.

clue.text: I book in less transport for children?

indicators.note: in puts I and the letter for book inside the word for less

parts.note: minus means less, as in five minus two

explanation.surface: Someone reserving fewer seats on a school run.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: a minibus is a small bus, so a 'mini' vehicle as if for little ones.
explanation.definitionFit: A minibus is a small passenger van, often used for school trips.

clue.text: RN names misused could be bad

indicators.note: misused means the letters of RN and names are put into the wrong order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Royal Navy names used carelessly might cause offence.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the answer's adjective: bad manners.
explanation.definitionFit: Manners are social conduct, which can be good or bad behaviour.

clue.text: Carpet laid out for one celebrated down under

parts.note: a mat is a small carpet

indicators.note: laid out means the letters of laid are set out afresh in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A rug spread out for an Australian celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: Matilda is celebrated in the Australian song Waltzing Matilda, where she is a swagman's bedroll.
explanation.definitionFit: Waltzing Matilda, the unofficial national song of Australia, names its swag roll Matilda.

clue.text: A disciplinarian, I rant terribly in a police force

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the name of the police force

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

indicators.note: terribly says the letters of I and rant are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A strict officer confesses to shouting wildly within the force.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'A' belongs to the definition, while the 'a' before 'police force' is only a link; the Met is the usual crossword police force.
explanation.definitionFit: A martinet is a strict enforcer of rules, named after a French drill-master.

clue.text: Relish nothing in a dance

parts.note: tang is a sharp flavour, relish
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Savouring nothing during a dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The tango is a ballroom dance from Argentina.

clue.text: Accountant has credit in the capital

indicators.note: has ... in means the accountant's letters hold the credit abbreviation inside

parts.note: ACA is an Associate of the Institute of Chartered Accountants
CR is the bookkeeping abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper has money owed to them in the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Accra is the capital city of Ghana.

clue.text: Shut tight

explanation.surface: Tightly closed.
explanation.definitionFit: To close a door is to shut it; close also means near or tight-fitting, as in a close fit.

clue.text: Ugly old woman — one often getting stoned!

explanation.surface: A hag who is frequently intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stoned' suggests drugs, but farmers throw stones at the bird to scare it from crops.
explanation.definitionFit: An unattractive old woman is called an old crow; the black bird is a frequent target of stone-throwing farmers.

clue.text: Head of government in check — that's the rule

indicators.note: in puts that letter inside the word for check

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain

indicators.note: Head of picks the first letter of government

explanation.surface: Restraining the leader of the government is the principle.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch's reign is their period of rule.

clue.text: You get extra after indian dish in this US city

indicators.note: after puts the word for extra behind the dish

parts.note: a balti is a curry cooked in a wok-like pan, popular in Britain
more means extra

explanation.surface: Someone is promised second helpings after their curry in a US city.
explanation.walkthrough: A balti is a Birmingham-born style of curry.
explanation.definitionFit: Baltimore is a major port city in Maryland.

clue.text: Scoff after PC operating system in place with a view

indicators.note: after puts the word for scoff behind the system

parts.note: Windows is Microsoft's operating system for PCs
to scoff is British slang for eating greedily

explanation.surface: Eating after booting up the computer in a room with a vista.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoff' looks like mockery, but in British slang it means to eat greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat next to a window, as on a train or plane, gives a view outside.

clue.text: Small English county to which people may retire

explanation.surface: A little English shire where people go to settle in old age.
explanation.walkthrough: Beds is the short form of Bedfordshire, a county north of London; 'retire' also means going to bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Beds is the abbreviated name of Bedfordshire; at night people retire to their bed.
